recipes.name: Chocolate-Filled Crescents
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) can Pillsbury® refrigerated crescent dinner rolls

steps.text: Heat oven to 350 degrees F. Separate dough into 8 triangles.
Place tablespoon of chocolate chips on wide end of each triangle. Roll up, starting at shortest side of triangle, rolling to opposite point. Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350 degrees F. for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown. Sprinkle with powdered sugar.

review.reviewBody: I made this into chocolate-marshmallow crescents by adding three mini marshmallows into the middle of the crescents over the mini chocolate chips. The boys inhaled them. Big hit.

I made these using Hershey's Special Dark Chocolate chips and some left over Carnation Dulce De Luche Caramel. I omitted the powdered sugar. First, spread a thin layer of the caramel on the crescent triangle and top with the chips across the lower half. Roll. Bake on parchment paper (because the caramel may ooze out a little). 
Very tasty!!

I found this recipe in a Hershey's cookbook when I was a kid. My Mom and I made these together using regular size milk chocolate chips instead of mini chips. Before we put the chips on the croissant, we sprinkled cinnamon and sugar, then put the chips, then rolled it up. Since then, I have been hooked--and now make them for my husband who loves them. Did I mention that eating one straight out the oven with the chocolate warm and melting and a glass of cold milk is just heavenly? ENJOY!

I used the Grands Crescent rolls with pieces of chocolate from a big candy bar. Put 2 pieces of dough together, put 2 pieces of chocolate on the dough, about 1/2" apart. Took one end of dough folded over chocolate. Did the same other side .Looks like a hot pocket. Baked 350 oven for about 13 minutes. While still warm, I put chocolate cream cookie spread on top. Chocolate pieces melted just right. EAT WARM!

I like the concept of these treats. I recommend using a high quality milk chocolate chip in this recipe. I decided to get out my Guittard Milk Chocolate chips and I paired that with creamy honey roasted peanut butter - adding a small dollop of the peanut butter to the unbaked dough, placed chocolate chips on top and gave it a light sprinkle of cinnamon before rolling it up to bake. I found that mine lightly browned by 10 minutes. Make sure you keep an eye on these as you don't want them to get too browned!

Yummy. Couldn't have been better or easier. I made 3 different versions. I wanted to be able to rate the original recipe, so I made some that way (only I didn't have mini chocolate chips, so I chopped some regular), I also read some of the reviews that suggested cream cheese, which sounded yummy, so I added 3 oz. cream cheese to about 1/2 of the chocolate chips. I used half of that on 2 crescents, then added a handful of chopped walnuts to the final 2 crescents. All 3 versions were yummy. What a versitale recipe!
They taste delicious. I used full sized dark chocolate chips and folded the ends of the dough closed.

I make these with the funsize Milkyways. Wrap the crescent all the way around the milkyway so the chocolate does not ooze out. Brush with a little butter. (I use spray butter) top with a sprinkle of powdered sugar. Yum

10-11-2017 I made these into witches’ hats for Halloween. 10-12-2012 Oh my! This is bad! No, no, no, I mean this recipe is delicious! What's bad is that I can have a chocolate fix so quickly and easily! I sprinkled a few with confectioner's sugar and topped the rest with chocolate striping and chopped pecans. Now I have to make myself not eat every single one!

Yum, yum, yum! These are so easy to get together and decadent! I mixed some softened cream cheese with a little powdered sugar and spread a thin layer on the crescent triangle. I then added the chocolate chips and slightly pressed into the cream cheese. I rolled from the big end and made sure the open ends were facing up once rolled. This recipe is so versatile! You could fill with just about anything. I think some nutella and chopped hazelnuts would be amazing! Give these a try!
I made this for Christmas Eve, but I added Nutella before sprinkling on the mini chocolate chips. It was a hit at our gathering!
I made them exactly as written with organic crescent rolls and dark chocolate chips. Super easy to make. The family loved them.
Grandson's favorite. I just close the sides to keep all the gooey chocolate inside the roll.
A good idea but not too tasty.
I used nutella instead of chocolate chips! I filled some with pecans and some with cherries
Well that wasn’t good at all.
It needs a cream filling, kinda bland
I also added Nutella and chopped walnuts. Big hit!
I made some with pumpkin cream cheese and chocolate chips and I made some with chocolate chips and peanut butter chips. They are fantastic.
These tasted every bit as good as those bought at a nearby coffee shop. I think, though, they are much better, brushed with a simple glaze. The powdered sugar alone didn't add much.
